**Root Cause Summary:**
- The `reindex` main container **completed successfully** on Wednesday at `02:41:17Z` (exit 0, logged `"reindex complete in 41m11s, exiting 0"`).
- The `cloud-sql-proxy` is defined as a **regular app container**, not a Kubernetes-native sidecar. It has been running continuously since `02:00:05Z` on Wednesday and never terminated when the main container finished.

input.note:
**Root Cause:** The `cloud-sql-proxy` container in the `catalog-reindex` Job pod is a regular app container — not a Kubernetes-native sidecar — so it does not terminate when the main `reindex` container finishes. This left Job `catalog-reindex-29654040` stuck in an Active state, and because the CronJob uses `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`, the Thursday and Friday nightly runs were skipped [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/cron-jobs#concurrency-policy-0].

**Evidence:**
- Pod `catalog-reindex-29654040-v8m2q` shows `ready_containers: 1/2` and `status: NotReady`.
- Container `reindex` is `Terminated (Completed), exit code 0, finished 2026-05-20T02:41:17Z`. Logs confirm: `"reindex complete in 41m11s, exiting 0"`.
- Container `cloud-sql-proxy` is still `Running since 2026-05-20T02:00:05Z` (over 2 days ago).
- CronJob status shows `active: [catalog-reindex-29654040]` — the Job is still considered running, so new runs are blocked [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/cron-jobs#concurrency-policy-0].

**Immediate Fix:**
Delete the stuck Job (`catalog-reindex-29654040`) in the `search` namespace. This will terminate the pod (including the lingering `cloud-sql-proxy` container) and mark the Job as no longer active. The CronJob will then be free to create a new Job at the next scheduled time (tonight at 02:00). If you need the index refreshed sooner, you can manually create a Job from the CronJob spec (`kubectl create job --from=cronjob/catalog-reindex manual-reindex -n search`).

**Permanent Fix:**
Move the `cloud-sql-proxy` container from `.spec.template.spec.containers` into `.spec.template.spec.initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`. This makes it a Kubernetes-native sidecar container. Native sidecar containers do not prevent a Job from completing — the kubelet will automatically terminate them once the last main container has finished [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/sidecar-containers#jobs-with-sidecar-containers-0]. The cluster is running kubelet v1.30.4, which fully supports this feature. Example structure:

```yaml
initContainers:
  - name: cloud-sql-proxy
    image: gcr.io/cloud-sql-connectors/cloud-sql-proxy:2.11.4
    restartPolicy: Always   # ← this makes it a sidecar
    args: ["--port=5432", "acme-prod:us-central1:catalog-db"]
```
[cite: concepts/workloads/pods/sidecar-containers#jobs-with-sidecar-containers-1]
